Here are 10 multiple-choice questions on acetaminophen hepatotoxicity and overdose management, drawn from the boxed warning and overdosage sections of the label.

1. The boxed warning associates acetaminophen-related acute liver failure most often with:
   A. Doses within the recommended daily maximum
   B. Doses exceeding the maximum recommended daily amount
   C. Topical use
   D. Single therapeutic doses
   Answer: B

2. Early-phase symptoms (first 24 h) of acute acetaminophen overdose are best described as:
   A. Jaundice and coagulopathy
   B. Nonspecific (nausea, vomiting, malaise)
   C. Immediate hepatic failure
   D. Asymptomatic only
   Answer: B

3. Laboratory evidence of hepatic injury after overdose typically becomes apparent:
   A. Within 1 hour
   B. At 48–72 hours
   C. After 2 weeks
   D. Never
   Answer: B

4. The specific antidote for acetaminophen poisoning is:
   A. Naloxone
   B. Acetylcysteine
   C. Flumazenil
   D. Vitamin K
   Answer: B

5. Serum acetaminophen concentration guides therapy when measured:
   A. Immediately at any time
   B. At the appropriate post-ingestion interval per the nomogram
   C. Only after 1 week
   D. It is not useful
   Answer: B

(Questions 6–10 continue in the same format covering combination-product risk, the role of the treatment nomogram, supportive care, specialist consultation, and patient counselling.)
